excerpt: Autonomous AI Research and Development: The ability to either: (1) Fully automate the work of an entry-level remote-only Researcher at Anthropic, as assessed by performance on representative tasks or (2) cause dramatic acceleration in the rate of effective scaling.
paraphrase: The Autonomous AI R&D threshold covers either full automation of an entry-level researcher's work or causing dramatic acceleration in effective scaling rates.

excerpt: Specifically, this would be the case if we observed or projected an increase in the effective training compute of the world's most capable model that, over the course of a year, was equivalent to two years of the average rate of progress during the period of early 2018 to early 2024.
paraphrase: This threshold is triggered by an observed or projected year of scaling equivalent to two years of the 2018-2024 average progress rate.
stated_bar: two years of the average rate of progress during 2018 to 2024

excerpt: We roughly estimate that the 2018-2024 average scaleup was around 35x per year, so this would imply an actual or projected one-year scaleup of 35^2 = ~1000x.
paraphrase: Given an estimated 35x/year average scaleup, the threshold implies roughly a 1000x one-year scaleup.

excerpt: Model Autonomy checkpoint: The ability to perform a wide range of advanced software engineering tasks autonomously that could be precursors to full autonomous replication or automated AI R&D, and that would take a domain expert human 2-8 hours to complete.
paraphrase: The Model Autonomy checkpoint covers autonomous performance of advanced software engineering tasks, taking a human expert 2-8 hours, that could precede full autonomy or automated R&D.

excerpt: We primarily view this level of model autonomy as a checkpoint on the way to managing the risks of robust, fully autonomous systems with capabilities that might include (a) automating and greatly accelerating research and development in AI development (b) generating their own revenue and using it to run copies of themselves in large-scale, hard-to-shut-down operations.
paraphrase: This checkpoint is viewed as a step toward managing risks from fully autonomous systems capable of accelerating AI R&D or self-funding large-scale self-replication.

excerpt: The 35x/year scaleup estimate is based on assuming the rate of increase in compute being used to train frontier models from ~2018 to May 2024 is 4.2 x/year (reference), the impact of increased (LLM) algorithmic efficiency is roughly equivalent to a further 2.8 x/year (reference), and the impact of post training enhancements is a further 3 x/year (informal estimate).
paraphrase: The 35x/year estimate combines a 4.2x/year compute increase, 2.8x/year algorithmic efficiency gain, and 3x/year post-training enhancement.

excerpt: Combined, these have an effective rate of scaling of 35 x/year.
paraphrase: Combined, the estimated factors yield an effective scaling rate of 35x/year.

excerpt: September 19, 2023 RSP-2023 (aka RSP v1.0): Initial version.
paraphrase: The changelog records the initial RSP version dated September 19, 2023.

excerpt: October 15, 2024 RSP-2024: This update introduces a more flexible and nuanced approach to assessing and managing AI risks while maintaining our commitment not to train or deploy models unless we have implemented adequate safeguards.
paraphrase: The October 15, 2024 update introduces a more flexible risk management approach while retaining the commitment to adequate safeguards before training or deployment.

excerpt: Key improvements include new capability thresholds to indicate when we should upgrade our safeguards, refined processes for evaluating model capabilities and the adequacy of our safeguards (inspired by safety case methodologies), and new measures for internal governance and external input.
paraphrase: Key improvements include new capability thresholds, refined evaluation processes inspired by safety cases, and new internal governance and external input measures.

excerpt: We describe the most notable changes below.
paraphrase: The following entries describe the most notable changes.

excerpt: ASL definition changed: The term "ASL" now refers to groups of technical and operational safeguards (it previously also referred to models). We also introduced the new concepts of Capability Thresholds and Required Safeguards.
paraphrase: The ASL term now refers only to safeguard groups rather than models, and new concepts of Capability Thresholds and Required Safeguards were introduced.

excerpt: This change allows for more targeted application of safeguards based on specific capabilities, rather than broad model categories.
paraphrase: The redefinition enables safeguards to be targeted at specific capabilities instead of broad model categories.

locator: Changelog / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
excerpt: ARA threshold now a checkpoint: We replaced our previous autonomous replication and adaption (ARA) threshold with a "checkpoint" for autonomous AI capabilities.
paraphrase: The former ARA threshold was replaced with a checkpoint concept for autonomous AI capabilities.

locator: Changelog / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
excerpt: Rather than triggering higher safety standards automatically, reaching this checkpoint will prompt additional evaluation of the model's capabilities and accelerate our preparation of stronger safeguards.
paraphrase: Reaching the checkpoint now triggers additional evaluation and accelerated safeguard preparation rather than automatic escalation.
